{{Current events header|2016|06|28}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**Three [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant]] bombings in [[Yemen|Yemen's]] southern port city of [[Al Mukalla]] kill 38 government forces and injure 24 others. [http://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-idUSKCN0ZD292 (Reuters)]
*[[Iraqi Civil War (2014–present)|Iraqi Civil War ]]
**At least 12 people are killed and 32 more are injured in a suicide bombing in [[Baghdad]]. [http://www.rferl.org/content/twelve-killed-suicide-bombing-mosque-abu-ghraib-near-baghdad-islamic-state/27824606.html (Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty)]
*[[2016 Istanbul airport attack|Atatürk Airport attack]]
**Suspected  [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] militants attack  [[Turkey]]'s [[Istanbul Atatürk Airport]]. A senior Turkish government official says nearly 50 people are killed and 88 are injured. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-36658187 (BBC)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2016/jun/28/turkey-airport-explosions-ataturak-istanbul (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.thestar.com/news/world/2016/06/28/explosions-rock-istanbul-airport-say-turkish-officials.html (AP via ''Toronto Star'')], [http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/world/istanbul-airport-attack-several-killed-in-explosions/news-story/b4e50bc0f121945dcba758ac1b2fe24f?utm_source=feedburner&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=Feed%3A%20TheAustralianNewsNDM%20(The%20Australian%20%7C%20News%20%7C) (''The Australian'')]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Al-Bukamal Offensive]]
***Rebels of the [[New Syrian Army]] begin an offensive to capture the eastern town of [[Al-Bukamal]], currently held by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] militants. [http://www.rferl.org/content/syrian-rebels-recapturing-islamic-state-town/27826764.html (Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty)]

;Business and economics
*[[Volkswagen emissions scandal]]
**[[Volkswagen Group|Volkswagen]] and the [[United States Department of Justice|United States Justice Department]] agree on a $14.7 billion settlement for its [[Emission standard|emissions-cheating]] program. The breakdown: $10 billion to consumers to cover buybacks and fixes; $2 billion for  green energy funds investment; and, $2.7 billion to offset diesel emissions. In addition, VW agrees on a settlement with  44 U.S. states, the [[Washington, D.C.|District of Columbia]], and [[Puerto Rico]] that will cost at least $600 million. As for Europe, Volkswagen says its diesel vehicles don't violate [[European Union]] emissions standards. [http://www.reuters.com/article/us-volkswagen-emissions-settlement-idUSKCN0ZD2S5 (Reuters)] [http://www.nasdaq.com/article/vw-is-set-for-near15-billion-emissions-settlement-20160628-00272 (Nasdaq)]
*[[IKEA]] is to recall 27 million Malm chests of drawers in North America due to the danger they pose to children. Since 2014, at least three children have died when the drawers toppled over on them. [http://www.bbc.com/news/business-36648589 (BBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[EgyptAir Flight 804]]
**One of the flight recorders of EgyptAir Flight 804 has been fully repaired in [[Paris]] after being found in the [[Mediterranean Sea]] and will now be sent to [[Egypt]] to be analyzed. [http://www.euronews.com/2016/06/28/flight-recorder-of-crashed-egyptair-flight-is-repaired/ (Euronews)]
*Three crew members are missing and one worker is injured following the head-on collision of two [[BNSF Railway]] freight trains  near the American town of [[Panhandle, Texas]]. Officials, concerned that flames from box car fires could cause a fast-moving grass fire, order an evacuation of some nearby areas. [http://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/3-missing-1-injured-in-head-on-train-collision-in-texas/ar-AAhJaBR?li=BBnb7Kz&ocid=edgsp (AP via MSN)]
*A huge explosion completely destroys a house and damages 24 others in [[Mississauga]], [[Canada]]. At least one person is dead and 9 others are injured, according to [[Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services]]. [http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/mississauga-house-explosion-1.3656811 (CBC News)]

;International relations
*[[Bolivia]], [[Ethiopia]], [[Kazakhstan]], and [[Sweden]] are elected to be non-permanent members in the [[United Nations Security Council]]. [http://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/sweden-wins-seat-security-council-ballot-40190680 (ABC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[United Kingdom withdrawal from the European Union]]
**The European Parliament's first debate on the UK's vote to leave is marked by bitter exchanges as prominent pro-Brexit figure [[Nigel Farage]] is booed and heckled by members of the [[European Parliament]] and European Commission President [[Jean-Claude Juncker]] is heckled after saying that he is neither a robot nor a bureaucrat. [http://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-eu-referendum-36648664 (BBC)]
**[[Labour Party (UK)|Labour party]] leader [[Jeremy Corbyn]] refuses to resign after losing a vote of no confidence, with 80% of voting members of the [[Parliamentary Labour Party]] voting against him. Critics which include fellow [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|MP]]s cite his failure to do more in the effort for the UK to remain in the EU as the main issue. [http://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2016/jun/28/brexit-live-cameron-eu-leaders-brussels-corbyn-confidence (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[David Cameron]] will turn over his office no later than 9 September 2016. [http://www.dailymail.co.uk/news/article-3663868/Wish-weren-t-Dave-Latest-humiliation-PM-arrives-Brussels-explain-let-Brexit-happen-EU-hastily-runs-Union-flag.html (''Daily Mail'')]
**[[First Minister of Scotland|Scotland's First Minister]] [[Nicola Sturgeon]] schedules a meeting Wednesday with  [[President of the European Parliament|European Parliament President]] [[Martin Schulz]] about remaining in the EU, and intends  to discuss the Scottish issue with the [[European Commission]]. [http://time.com/4385307/brexit-nicola-sturgeon-referendum-scotland-martin-schulz-eu/ (''Time'')] [http://www.reuters.com/article/us-britain-eu-scotland-idUSKCN0ZE1HR (Reuters)]
*Following a [[Constitutional Court of South Africa|South African Constitutional Court]] order, the [[National Treasury (South Africa)|National Treasury]] reports [[President of South Africa|President]] [[Jacob Zuma]] should pay back $500,000, the public funds spent upgrading his private residence. [http://gulfnews.com/news/africa/south-africa/zuma-told-to-pay-back-500-000-in-public-funds-1.1853930 (Gulf News)] [http://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/zuma-should-pay-back-500-000-of-public-funds-sa-treasury-116062701099_1.html (''Business Standard'')]
;Science and technology
*[[Durham University|Durham]] and [[Oxford College of Emory University|Oxford universities']] [[Geology|geologists]], working with  a helium exploration company, discover an at least 54 billion cubic foot field of [[helium]] in the [[Tanzania]]n [[East African Rift|East African Rift Valley]]. Previously, helium  has only been found in small quantities. This field, found using a new exploration approach connected to [[Volcano|volcanic activity]], could potentially meet global demand for several years. This research is being presented  to the Goldschmidt geochemistry conference in [[Yokohama]], [[Japan]]. [http://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-36651048 (BBC)] [http://phys.org/news/2016-06-huge-helium-discovery-life-saving.html (Phys.org)] [http://goldschmidt.info/2016/ (Goldschmidt conference)]
